record.text: This is one area where Cybertrucks are ahead. They’ve had knobs in the driver’s seat the whole time.
After selling a screenless tracker as a way to cut distractions, Google may be ready to put a display back on your wrist.

external.description:
Earlier this year, Google Fitbit Air was pitched as a health tracker for people trying to avoid the distractions that come with screens. Now, Google seems to be going in the opposite direction with its next tracker, the Fitbit Edge.

The contradiction is that the tracker allegedly comes with a screen, according to reports from Android Headlines. From leaked images, the Fitbit Edge looks a lot like the Fitbit Charge, which Google last updated in 2023. That suggests that the Edge could be its successor.

It also reportedly has a small display, GPS, notifications, and limited app support.

Fitbit Air vs Whoop 5.0Which screenless fitness tracker is actually worth buying?TechloyOgbonda Chivumnovu

## What the Fitbit Edge is

The Fitbit Edge looks like a mid-range fitness tracker that could sit between the $99 Fitbit Air and the $399 Pixel Watch 5. It's rumoured to have a small screen, GPS, an altimeter and limited app support for things like Google Maps, YouTube Music and Find My Phone.

Image credit: Android Headlines

It may also offer up to seven days of battery life, automatic activity detection, and work with both Android and iOS. That last part matters because the Pixel Watch 5 is Android-only.

## Why Google is taking a different strategy with the Fitbit Edge

Google's pitch for the Fitbit Air was simple: less screen, fewer distractions. The company positioned it as a screenless tracker that lets people check their health data on their phone while staying notification-free when they want to focus.

The Fitbit Edge, though, does the opposite. It adds a screen, notifications, and even some apps.

But the thing is, Google is still a business. Even though the screenless market is real, it's still quite niche. Whoop and Oura have their audiences, but many people still want to see their stats on their wrist. And the data makes that clear; the IDC expects 159.7 million smartwatches to ship globally in 2026, compared with 40.2 million wristbands. That's roughly four times as many smartwatches as wristbands.

record.text: This ranking compares eight providers of branded digital banking solutions. They offer different combinations of software and regulated services.

external.description:
A digital banking demo usually begins with the customer app. An account appears, a payment is sent and a card is frozen in a few taps. The harder questions come afterward: who holds the account, where is the transaction recorded, how does an operations team resolve a failed payment, and what happens when the business adds another provider?

This ranking compares **eight providers of branded digital banking solutions**. They offer different combinations of software and regulated services. The order reflects their relevance to fintechs seeking a branded customer experience, operational tools and connections to financial service providers. It does not represent a score for reliability, price or customer satisfaction.

## **Eight white label banking platforms at a glance**

The table describes each provider’s published product focus. A buyer should confirm the exact modules, integrations, regulated services and commercial terms offered for its project.

Rank| Provider| Published focus| Most relevant buyer
---|---|---|---
1| FinHost| Branded apps, back office, banking modules and third-party integrations| Fintechs building a multi-service product with selected partners
2| Crassula| Branded banking apps, back office and financial product modules| Teams launching accounts, payments and cards together
3| SDK.finance| Configurable fintech core with ready web and mobile interfaces| Teams planning extensive product and technical customisation
4| Velmie| Banking software, branded channels and integration orchestration| Teams combining banking functions across providers
5| ConnectPay| White label neobank services through a regulated provider and APIs| Teams seeking a technology and regulated service arrangement
6| OpenWay| Way4 payments, wallets, cards and digital banking technology| Institutions with a strong payments or card focus
7| Backbase| Digital banking experiences connected to existing systems| Banks modernising customer and employee channels
8| Temenos| Digital banking and core banking products| Established institutions planning a larger technology programme

## **1. FinHost: a branded platform for connected financial services**

FinHost’s white label banking platform combines web and mobile applications, a back office, banking functions and integrations with external providers. Its published offering covers customer journeys involving accounts, payments, cards and, where relevant, crypto services. 

Its relevance lies in bringing the customer interface and operational work into one proposed architecture. FinHost also offers a source code licence for businesses that need a different model for customisation and deployment. The rights, delivery scope and maintenance responsibilities under that option should be established in the contract. 

**Test beyond the demo:** Ask FinHost to trace a payment from the customer app through the relevant partner, transaction records and back office. Then ask the team to show how a failed or delayed payment is investigated.

## **2. Crassula: apps and operations around a banking product**

Crassula presents a white label solution with branded web and mobile applications, a back office and modules for building digital banking products. Its materials describe connections to banking partners and functions such as accounts, payments and cards. 

Crassula is a close comparison for a fintech planning several services within one app. As with any platform that connects to external providers, the buyer needs to identify which capabilities are supplied by Crassula and which depend on partner agreements.

**Test beyond the demo:** Request a walkthrough of onboarding, payment review, fee changes and reconciliation in the proposed configuration.

## **3. SDK.finance: a configurable fintech core**

SDK.finance describes a white label digital banking platform with a transactional backend, web and mobile interfaces, back office tools and APIs. Its offering is relevant to teams that expect to adapt product logic and connect a range of financial providers.

Buyers should examine how much of the planned product can be configured using existing components and how much requires implementation work. That distinction affects both the project scope and the team needed after launch.

**Test beyond the demo:** Ask the provider to change a fee, limit or approval rule in a test environment, then show how the change appears in the app, records and operations tools.

record.text: Amazon is putting the former Copilot CTO on its workplace AI assistant Quick and coding tool Kiro.

external.description:
Looking at where the AI industry is headed, the AI agent era is clearly here, and Amazon isn't willing to let the opportunity slip by.

For years, the shopping platform has built AI products to help users manage tasks while making workflows easier by automating them.

Now, the retail giant is looking to turn its AI investments into used products by expanding its AI agent Offerings. This, the company is doing to compete with Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, both of which have gained traction in recent months.

Why Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Quit, and Who AgreedCoxon’s warning comes as both OpenAI and Anthropic have faced incidents involving their AI systems gaining access to other organisations’ systems.TechloyDavid Adubiina

## How Amazon plans to compete

Amazon Web Services (AWS), the company's cloud computing division, has hired Pedram Rezaei, the CTO of Microsoft Copilot, to help the e-commerce and cloud giant build out its agentic AI business.

According to details revealed by a Business Insider report, Rezaei will initially work on Quick and Kiro, two of Amazon's products central to its AI agent strategy.

Quick is AWS's AI assistant and productivity app launched in early 2026 as the successor to Amazon Q Business. Unlike Amazon Quick, which is a broad, cross-application AI assistant designed to connect files and business workflows, Kiro is a specialized, agentic AI-powered IDE focused on structured software engineering.

According BI report, both have seen their user base grow, with Quick's monthly AI users increasing fourfold from the first quarter to the second. Kiro, meanwhile, has its user base doubling over the same period.

These two sit within a wider portfolio that Amazon has been building, including its Bedrock model platform, coding assistants and other agentic software.

record.text: The Watcher’ Season 2 brings Naomi Watts back to Netflix

external.description:
Naomi Watts and Bobby Cannavale return as the Brannocks four years after Season 1.

As the wait between TV seasons gets longer, four years doesn’t seem all that crazy anymore. It’s funny to think back to what the world was like when the first season of “The Watcher ” dropped on Netflix back in 2022. Argentina won the World Cup, ChatGPT was just launching, and we were all slowly coming out of the COVID daze. And if you remember this show and have been waiting for Season 2 news, you’re in luck! It’s happening: Naomi Watts and Bobby Cannavale are back, and things will pick up after the events of Season 1. Here’s everything you need to know about the second season of “The Watcher.”

Everything you need to know about ‘The Watcher’ Season 2

When does ‘The Watcher’ Season 2 come out? Can you watch ‘The Watcher’ Season 2 for free? What is ‘The Watcher’ Season 2 about? Who stars in ‘The Watcher’ Season 2?

Sign Up

$8.99+ / month netflix.com

When does ‘The Watcher’ Season 2 come out?

There’s no exact date yet for when Season 2 of “The Watcher ” will drop, but the show is officially in production. Filming is underway, according to Netflix, in New York, so I would expect a late 2027 release.

Can you watch ‘The Watcher’ Season 2 for free once it starts streaming?

Not right now, no. Netflix doesn’t currently offer a free trial in the U.S., so you can’t watch “The Watcher” Season 2 for free. But Netflix is testing free trials in other countries , so it’s not impossible that by the time the second season drops that free trial has come here. It’s sure to be big news if it does. If that doesn’t happen, you’ll need a subscription to watch “The Watcher.” Plans start at $9 per month with ads (that’s what I have), and the ad-free plan jumps to $20 per month.

Sign Up

netflix.com

Netflix

Netflix is a leading subscription-based video streaming service that offers on-demand access to an extensive library of over 3,000 movies, 2,000+ TV shows, and a growing collection of acclaimed Netflix originals. Renowned for producing groundbreaking content, Netflix has become a cultural powerhouse with hit originals like “Stranger Things,” “Wednesday,” “Squid Game,” “The Crown,” “Tiger King,” “Bridgerton,” “The Witcher,” and “Black Mirror.”

…

The platform constantly updates its catalog, introducing fresh content alongside timeless classics and international hits. Netflix’s commitment to storytelling has also earned critical acclaim, with award-winning exclusives such as “Roma,” “Marriage Story,” “The Power of the Dog,” “Mank,” and “Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom.” In 2023, their animated film “Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio” won an Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, further solidifying Netflix’s reputation for high-quality content.

Recently, Netflix has expanded beyond standard movies and TV titles with the addition of video podcasts , and is also exploring a digital store that would offer third-party streamers within the app.

Netflix offers three plans – stream on 2 devices in HD with the “Standard with Ads” ($8.99) plan, on 2 devices in HD with the “Standard” ($19.99) plan, and 4 devices in up to 4K on the “Premium” ($26.99) plan.

Sign Up

$8.99+ / month

netflix.com

What is ‘The Watcher’ Season 2 about?

Spoiler Alert. There are spoilers below for Season 1 of ‘The Watcher.’

Netflix hasn’t shared much, but what we do know is that “The Watcher ” Season 2 will pick up with the Brannocks after Season 1’s very ambiguous ending. For those who forgot what this show is about (who could blame you!), Nora and Dean (Watts and Cannavale) move into their dream home in the wealthy neighborhood of Westfield, New Jersey and start getting terrorizing letters from someone calling themselves “The Watcher.” This person has been watching the house for years and seems to know too much about the Brannocks and their kids. Dean basically becomes obsessed with finding out who “The Watcher” really is… and his obsession eventually tears the family apart.

Netflix hasn’t revealed what brings the family back into the mystery or where the story goes next. And that’s fair considering this is based on a real-life case that’s still unsolved. That means creators Ryan Murphy, Ian Brennan, and company can pretty much take this wherever they want now, and after four years, they’ve had plenty of time to surprise us!

Who stars in ‘The Watcher’ Season 2?

Naomi Watts and Bobby Cannavale are both coming back for “The Watcher ” Season 2 as Nora and Dean Brannock. Isabel Gravitt also returns as their daughter Ellie, while Margo Martindale is back as the unsettling neighbor Maureen “Mo.” That’s it so far for the confirmed cast, but there’s always an opportunity for new neighbors to move in and expand the cast from Season 1. Ian Brennan is back as showrunner, with Ryan Murphy and Brennan both executive producing.

The Watcher

October 13, 2022

Ominous letters. Strange neighbors. Sinister threats. A family moves into their suburban dream home, only to discover they’ve inherited a nightmare.
